newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
UNITED FRONT'S BID TO CAPTURE POWER IN UTTAR PRADESH
SUFFERS
United Front's (UF) bid to keep the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) out of power in Uttar Pradesh is facing problems.

The political rivalry between Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Mulayam Singh Yadav and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leader Mayawati has emerged as a major stumbling block. Given the poll outcome, UF cannot form the government without the support of both SP and BSP.
The Economic Times
GDP GROWTH IN 1995/96 LOWERED TO 6.3 PCT

The overall growth rate in the economy was revised from seven percent, stated in the Economic Survey update, to about 6.3 percent for 1995/96 (April-March). The estimate of seven percent Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth rate had gone off the mark primarily because agriculture production was over estimated. Agriculture has about 30 percent weightage in the GDP.
APRIL-JULY EXPORTS RISE 11.5 PCT; IMPORTS UP SIX PCT

Exports in dollar terms recorded an increase of 11.5 percent in April-July compared to 29.9 percent in the same period last year. Imports increased by six percent against 39.2 percent last year, according to the government's monthly economic report for September. Petroleum, oil and lubricants' (POL) imports increased by 42 percent while non-POL imports declined 2.4 percent in the same period. Foreign exchange reserves (excluding gold and SDRs), which stood at $17.04 million at the end of 1995/96 (April-March), increased by $925 million and stood at $17.97 million at the end of August 1996.
THIRD TRANCHE OF DIVESTMENT TO TAKE PLACE NEXT FISCAL

The third tranche of disinvestment of government equity in state owned firms may spill over into the next fiscal. The Disinvestment Commission will advise the department of public enterprises on industries where the government can offload equity in part or in full. There would not be significant divestment in firms to be categorised as global giants as the government has already decided on little or no divestment in core and strategic areas.
FOREIGN CURRENCY CONVERTIBLE BONDS BECOMING REDUNDANT

Foreign currency convertible bonds (FCCB) are fast becoming redundant. It is learnt that foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have stopped converting into equity their investments in Indian companies through FCCBs. Finance ministry sources said the trend could affect the economy at the macro level. The finance ministry encourages conversion of debt into equity so that the stock of external debt falls. Over $500 million worth of FCCBs were issued in fiscal 1993/94 (April-March) by companies in the form of debt with an offer of conversion into equity after three years.
STATES MAY HAVE TO FEND FOR THEMSELVES TO CUT DEFICIT

The Finance Ministry has set the Ninth Plan (1997-2002) outlay at 8,000 billion rupees (at 1996/97 prices) as against the Eighth Plan size of 4,340 billion rupees. This is 35 percent higher than the Eighth Plan outlay in real terms. Budgetary support for the Union sector will remain at the Eighth Plan level of 1,037 billion rupees. Government's assistance to states and Union Territories has been fixed at the Eighth Plan level of 785 billion and 62.5 billion rupees respectively.
MULTILATERAL WTO FRAMEWORK OPPOSED

India opposed a multilateral framework on investment under the World Trade Organisation. It also held that each member country must retain full competence to regulate and determine the role of foreign direct investment depending on its development priorities and strategies. But, India was of the view that all issues relating to the multilateral framework should be discussed and analysed in the UNCTAD.
CUT-OFF FOR 91 DAY PAPER SET AT 10.1 PCT

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a cut off yield of 10.1 percent on 91 day treasury bills. The auction received subscriptions of 9.68 billion rupees, almost twice the notified amount of five billion. Apart from the 42 competitive bids for the amount, RBI received two non-competitive bids totalling 2.75 billion rupees.
Financial Express
$100 MLN FOREX VIOLATIONS BY ITC ESTABLISHED

The Revenue Department has found evidence indicating violations of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) by ITC Ltd. The amount may run up to $100 million. Department officials, who visited the US for investigations, discovered transactions done by the company in its overseas deals in violation of FERA provisions. The transactions relate to invoicing, diversion of export earnings and transfer of illegal funds retained abroad by the company.
SOFTWARE EXPORTS CHANGE DIRECTION

The direction of software exports is shifting to Far-East Asia, South-East Asia and Africa. Exports to the Far-East and South-East Asia grew by 134 percent in rupee terms in 1995/96 (April-March). Exports to the new African markets in Zambia, Kenya and South Africa, grew by 66 percent. Comparatively, software exports to the United States declined from 70 percent to 61.82 percent in 1995/96.
Business Standard
STATE BANK CREDIT OFFTAKE DOWN IN FIRST HALF

State Bank of India (SBI) suffered a net decline in credit offtake in the first half of the current fiscal despite paring its prime lending rate (PLR) twice in three months. The two successive PLR cuts in July and September failed to stimulate the non-food credit offtake in the country's largest commercial bank. A net decline of 16 billion rupees in non-food credit between April and September, reflected a slow down in industrial activity, a SBI source said.
INFLATION NOT AT COST OF GROWTH: PLANNING COMMISSION

Planning Commission deputy chairman Madhu Dandavate cautioned against excessive monetary control measures. He said curbing of inflation should not be at the cost of industrial growth. Emphasising that there was no shortcut to increasing production, he said inflation could be checked only through increasing the rate of saving and controlling fiscal and revenue deficits.
FINANCIAL INSTITUITIONS SET TO MOP UP FUNDS

Financial institutions (FIs) have raised over 10 billion rupees through certificates of deposit and private placement of bonds in the past four weeks. This is seen as an indication that FIs are likely to mop up a large part of the funds that will be released through the expected cut in the cash reserve ratio (CRR). The central bank is expected to cut the CRR by at least one percentage point, thus releasing 40 billion rupees into the banking system.
Business Line
PETROLEUM CRISIS LOOMS LARGE

Supply of petroleum products may be disrupted in the coming months if the oil pool account deficit is not controlled soon. The Petroleum Ministry, cautioning the Prime Minister, said the oil pool account deficit, projected at 130 billion rupees by March 1997, may choke off supplies. The Ministry said the government may have to resort to demand management if the situation did not improve. It has recommended another price hike to avert the situation.
INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK PLANS CREDIT LINE

Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) is talking to leading merchant banks for offering market-making for its forthcoming 10 billion rupee bonds issue. IDBI is also discussing the building up a framework for offering market-making for the bonds. It is planned to extend a line of credit to the merchant banks with the drawable amount limited to the inventory which each one builds up. Selected merchant banks would have to offer two quotes for IDBI bonds at any point of time.
